previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, prior pancreas and kidney transplants, and a mechanical mitral valve was admitted with low-grade fever, whole-body pain, and abdominal discomfort following hemodialysis. Initial evaluation revealed an elevated INR of 6.7, which was managed with vitamin K and warfarin dose adjustments. A new left lower lobe infiltrate on chest X-ray prompted treatment with azithromycin for possible pneumonia, despite minimal respiratory symptoms. Abdominal pain was initially concerning for mesenteric ischemia or transplant rejection, but CT angiography showed patent mesenteric vessels and no evidence of ischemia; instead, significant fecal loading supported constipation as the primary cause. Pain was controlled with rectal morphine suppositories, which the patient tolerated well without nausea. The peritoneal dialysis catheter site showed no infection, and cultures were negative. She was discharged home with stable pain, resolved infection concerns, and a plan for close INR monitoring, bowel regimen optimization, and follow-up for a known right adnexal cyst and pleural effusion.

#Labile INR: Patient was found to have a subtherapeutic INR at 
2.0 (INR goal 3.0-3.5 for MVR) and was thus admitted for a 
heparin bridge. She remained subtherapeutic for approximately 3 
days on warfarin 5 mg daily. Her INR became supratherapeutic, 
most likely in the context of poor PO intake and per pharmacy 
there were no clear drug interactions. Her discharge INR was 
3.5. Patient was discharged on warfarin 2 mg daily and will f/u 
with HCA coagulation clinic.  
.
#Mechanical fall, pain control: Patient recently fell off of her 
horse and was evaluated at an OSH. She was discharged home with 
instructions to follow up with her PCP. She reported that her 
pain was relieved by tramadol and gabapentin. Unfortunately her 
pain was not adequately controlled with those medications. Her 
pain management was difficult given her ESRD and relative 
contraindications to a number of medications. She received po 
dilaudid and became extremely somnolent with a depressed 
respiratory rate. Her mental status subsequently improved with 
narcan. This occurred on a second occasion and at that time a CT 
head was performed which ruled out acute hemorrhage. Her mental 
status cleared with narcan. Throughout the course of her 
hospitalization she was able to function independently with a 
walker and with only minimal assistance from the nursing staff. 
Patient will apply for a home health aide to help her in the 
acute setting. Discharge pain regimen included acetaminophen, 
tramadol, and gabapentin. 

#AMS: Most likely toxic metabolic encephalopathy from medication 
side effects. Had multiple episodes of somnolence and confusion 
in the setting of opioid administration. Episodes resolved with 
narcan. Patient had two head CT scans to evaluate for acute 
hemorrhage in the setting of anticoagulation. Scans were 
negative for acute intracranial hemorrhage. Patient was 
mentating appropriately at discharge.
 
CHRONIC ISSUES
#ESRD: s/p DDRT and DDPT now with worsening renal function in 
the setting of chronic allofraft nephropathy. Received HD during 
her hospital stay. A PD catheter was recently placed and at this 
time the catheter is not fully functional. Her immunosuppresants 
were continued as well as the rest of her ESRD meds.

radiology_notes.text:
AP CHEST, 5:32 P.M., ___

HISTORY:  ___ woman with a failing kidney transplant, hypoxic, after
dialysis.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

Severe cardiomegaly is probably stable, but mild pulmonary edema, more
pronounced in the right lung is new, accompanied by at least small bilateral
pleural effusion.

Dual-channel right supraclavicular dialysis catheter set ends in the right
atrium.  Trans-subclavian atrial biventricular pacer defibrillator leads are
continuous from the right axillary power pack.  No pneumothorax.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with ESRD and somnolence after horseback riding
accident 2 days ago, on coumadin.  

COMPARISON:  NCHCT ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images were obtained through the brain
without administration of IV contrast.  Reformatted coronal and sagittal and
thin section bone algorithm reconstructed images were acquired.  

Total Exam DLP: 1026mGy-cm

CTDIvol: 63mGy

FINDINGS:

There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or large vascular
territory infarction.  The ventricles and sulci are normal in size and
configuration.  Periventricular white matter hypodensities of consistent with
sequela of chronic small vessel ischemic disease. The basal cisterns appear
patent and there is preservation of gray-white matter differentiation.  

No fracture is identified.  There is a left-sided mucous retention cyst in the
maxillary sinus and mild mucosal thickening in the right maxillary sinus.  The
paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities are otherwise
clear.  Note is made of a left globe prosthesis.  There are significant
diffuse vascular calcifications.  

IMPRESSION:

No acute intracranial abnormality.
